description:
Follow-up to JMAP-x2gd.81 (which hoisted ACCOUNT_ID/ACCOUNT_ID_B into common). The original .81 bead also suggested hoisting placeholder ids `"s0"|"c0"|"c1"|"e0"|"m0"|"b0"|"i0"|"s1"` as consts (CHAT_ID_C0, etc.), but that was scoped out of .81 because:

1. The placeholder ids `"s0"|"c0"|"e0"|"m0"|"b0"|"i0"` are RFC 8620 §5.3 create-record ephemeral client-chosen ids — they refer to objects WITHIN a single /set request and are arbitrary. They do not name stable identifiers. A const `CHAT_ID_C0 = "c0"` would imply more semantic stability than the wire shape carries.

2. The sibling test files (role_member_apply.rs, channel_category_apply.rs, etc.) use ONLY `ACCOUNT_ID` and `SPACE_ID` consts. They do NOT use `CHAT_ID_C0`-style consts. .81's primary engineering-basis was 'consistency with sibling files'; that consistency is now achieved.

3. `"s1"` in integration.rs appears 16 times as a magic-string `spaceId` field value in invite/ban/emoji subtests that do NOT seed any Space with id `"s1"`. The common module's `SPACE_ID = "s1"` const is used by sibling apply-test files where `"s1"` IS a seeded fixture's id. Importing `SPACE_ID` into integration.rs would conflate these two semantics — 'arbitrary placeholder' vs 'seeded fixture id'.

If this finding has value, the right shape is:
- New consts `SPACEID_PLACEHOLDER` (the magic-string used in subtests where no real Space is seeded) — different name from `SPACE_ID` to avoid the seeded-vs-placeholder ambiguity.
- Possibly: `CHAT_ID_C0`, `EMOJI_ID_E0`, `MSG_ID_M0`, `BAN_ID_B0`, `INVITE_ID_I0` for the per-target ephemeral placeholders (low confidence on value).

Engineering basis: cosmetic only. The variables already-named are clear in context (a `json!({"create": { "c0": ... }})` literal IS the create-record id). Filed at P4 to track whether downstream contributors find the longer-named consts more or less readable than the bare string literals.
title: tests: optional follow-up to JMAP-x2gd.81 — consider hoisting placeholder ids (s0/c0/e0/m0/b0/i0/s1) into named consts
